newsitem.title: NORWAY: Accounting gains boost Bergesen in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Accounting gains boost Bergesen in 1996.

text.p: Bergesen ASA, Norway's largest shipping company, reported 1996 profits far exceeding expectations Thursday, but the performance was primarily due to a change in accounting methods.

Bergesen posted pretax profits of 380 million crowns ($57.3 million) for 1996 compared with 489 million crowns ($73.4 million) a year ago and against an average forecast of about 150 million crowns ($22.5 million).
Operating profits surged to 575 million crowns ($86.3 million) from 277 million ($41.6 million) in 1995.

The company said, however, that a 25 percent extension of the depreciation period for tankers and dry bulk vessels -- to 25 years from 20 -- resulted in a reduction in depreciation charges of 153 million crowns ($23.0 million).
In addition, a new accounting principle had been implemented for costs of classification and drydocking.

"The operating profit would have been 75 million crowns ($11.3 million) weaker this year if last year's policy had been continued. The change in accounting principle also resulted in an extraordinary income of 61 million crowns ($9.2 million)," Bergesen said in a statement.
It later told a news conference that pretax profits would have been 91 million crowns ($13.7 million) under the old accounting system.
